parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional household survey with an unlabeled discrete choice experiment
parsed.population_and_sample: 344 randomly sampled households without in-house taps in the Nima-Maamobi informal settlement of Accra; an adult household head, spouse, or other adult responded.
parsed.exposure: Hypothetical household-tap service configurations varying in governance/provider (Accra Metropolitan Assembly versus Ghana Water Company Limited), connection fee, monthly bill, service days and hours, pressure, and water quality.
parsed.outcome: Household preferences and willingness to pay for a private household tap, including willingness to pay for provider type, connection, reliability, and other service attributes.
parsed.rationale: Sections 2.2-2.3 (pp. 572-573) identify the population, stratified sampling, 344 completed household surveys, and the choice experiment, whose attributes explicitly include the governing service provider and household-tap access conditions. Sections 4.3 and 5 (pp. 575-578) report empirical choice-model estimates showing preferences and willingness to pay for household connections, including a preference and payment premium for AMA rather than GWCL management.
